target: observe_push.sh — the batch carries _timestamp derived from each event's own ts, so a late/offline backfill indexes by when work happened, not when it uploaded
cmd:
mkdir -p .agentic/observability bin; printf '%s' '{"observability":{"enabled":true,"stack":{"enabled":true}}}' > .agentic/config.json; printf '%s
' '{"v":1,"ts":"2026-07-28T09:01:00Z","event":"shim_call","run_id":"r1"}' '{"v":1,"ts":"2026-07-30T14:30:00Z","event":"agent_stop","run_id":"r1"}' > .agentic/observability/events-20260728.jsonl; printf '#!/bin/sh
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in --data-binary) printf "%%s" "$2" > "$CAPTURE"; shift 2 ;; *) shift ;; esac; done
exit 0
' > bin/curl-cap; chmod +x bin/curl-cap; export O2_URL=http://localhost:5080 O2_AUTH=a:b CAPTURE="$PWD/sent.json"; O2_CURL="$PWD/bin/curl-cap" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/observe_push.sh" >/dev/null; jq -cs '.[0] | {n: length, first: (.[0] | {ts, _timestamp}), second: (.[1] | {ts, _timestamp})}' sent.json

provenance.note: 582 backfilled events all landed at the push instant; every dashboard time filter was answering 'when did I upload this?'
